figures.title: The national ANC cascade
figures.caption: Weighted attainment 77.6/52.4/19.2%; continuation 68% then 37%.

figures.title: Regional cascade decomposition
figures.caption: Regions with similar ANC8+ coverage lose women at opposite points.

figures.title: Continuation from 4 to 8 by circumstance
figures.caption: All women shown have already attended four times, so this isolates the cost of repeat attendance from initial demand.

figures.title: Development vs held-out AP
figures.caption: Mean development-to-held-out drop +0.076 AP -- the signature of selection over the same folds, not of a better model.

figures.title: Held-out calibration
figures.caption: Weighted decile means; the diagonal is perfect calibration.

figures.title: Repeated-split stability
figures.caption: Mean AP gain +0.0306 [+0.0179, +0.0434] over 20 independent splits.

figures.title: Paired stratified-PSU bootstrap
figures.caption: MLP (full pool) vs XGBoost (21 predictors); the AP interval includes zero, which is why the repeated-split evidence carries the claim.

figures.title: Global predictor importance
figures.caption: Exact additive attribution from the Explainable Boosting model; arrows give the direction of the dominant effect.

figures.title: Fitted shape functions
figures.caption: The exact learned curve for each top predictor, on the log-odds scale. Flat regions are values the model does not distinguish.

figures.title: Decision-curve analysis
figures.caption: Net benefit across plausible thresholds; the useful range is where the model sits above both default strategies.

figures.title: Subgroup discrimination
figures.caption: Several regional subgroups sit at or below chance; a national AUROC hides that. Subgroup n is small, so these are indicative.

figures.title: Systematic candidate screening
figures.caption: Every column of the Individual Recode screened on the development fold only; admission required the variable to be measured before or early in the pregnancy.

figures.title: Preprocessing ablation
figures.caption: The best variant buys +0.003 AP -- an order of magnitude less than the predictor set. Reported because a wins-only list would mislead.

figures.title: Hyperparameter sensitivity
figures.caption: Each bar moves one parameter away from the Optuna optimum with all others held; small bars mean the search bought little.

figures.title: Tuning gain over library defaults
figures.caption: Read against the ~0.08 development-to-held-out optimism gap: a tuning gain smaller than that is not evidence of better generalisation.

figures.title: Performance across the ladder
figures.caption: Development champion per rung, scored on held-out women. AP rises with prevalence and must never be compared across rungs; AUROC shows reaching care is easier to predict than completing it.

figures.title: Importance shift across the ladder
figures.caption: Green links: predictors that matter more as the threshold rises (engagement-limited); red: less (access-limited). Shares averaged over three independent importance methods.

figures.title: Domain roll-up across the ladder
figures.caption: Predictor importance aggregated into domains, normalised within rung, averaged over EBM, SHAP and drop-one.

figures.title: Regional performance against circumstance
figures.caption: Expected attainment predicted from wealth, education and household factors with region withheld; a positive gap means the region does better than its population profile implies.

figures.title: Modifiable versus fixed decomposition
figures.caption: Same folds, same model, three predictor subsets.

figures.title: Near-threshold risk bands
figures.caption: Women just below the operating threshold are the group a capacity-limited programme can realistically move.

figures.title: Importance before and after grouping duplicates
figures.caption: Travel time to hospital and residence are both present twice under different names, so per-column importance halves them.

figures.title: 21-predictor set vs the full pool (85 distinct, 95 columns)
figures.caption: Paired repeated splits; each dot is one split, the bar its mean. Logistic regression has almost nothing to tune, so it cannot favour a set through its hyperparameters.

figures.title: Each other candidate added, alone, to the 21-predictor set
figures.caption: Every bar is one of the 67 pool candidates outside the 21; teal bars clear +0.005 AP on at least 4 of 5 splits. Dashed line is the threshold.

figures.title: Stacking the additions onto the 21: a few carry the gain
figures.caption: Development AP as the 67 candidates are added in order of their individual gain; dashed line is the 21-predictor set alone; band is one SD across split seeds.

figures.title: Forward selection: the tiers, step by step
figures.caption: Each row adds one variable. Dark teal = tier 1 (reaches 90% of the full model's lift), light = tier 2 (each adds >= 0.005), grey = the first step that failed. Dashed = the 21-predictor set; dotted = the full pool. A selected set's development score is optimistic -- fig30 has the held-out view.

figures.title: Selection stability
figures.caption: Forward selection repeated on PSU-bootstrap resamples of the development set; below the dashed 70% line a variable's place is not reliable.

figures.title: On the held-out women: compact sets against the 21 and the full pool
figures.caption: AP above prevalence; each set fitted on development and scored once on held-out; bracketed counts are predictors. Paired bootstrap intervals against the 21 are in heldout_bootstrap.json -- most overlap zero.

figures.title: Tigray wartime difference-in-differences
figures.caption: Peaceful regions absorb the national trend and the extra recall error of older births (their within-region change is near zero); the remainder is the change associated with the war. Stratified PSU bootstrap intervals; robust to +/-3-month shifts of the war window.

figures.title: Regional gap, all births vs recent births
figures.caption: Expected attainment predicted with region withheld. The ranking is stable across the two windows, so it is not a period artefact.

figures.title: Drop-one within the 21-predictor set
figures.caption: Development AP lost when each member is removed from the 21 (fixed logistic regression at its own best regularisation, 5 split seeds). Grey = removing it costs nothing or helps. Ordered by ANC8+.

figures.title: Value by set size, within the 21 and from the full pool
figures.caption: Development AP above prevalence as a share of what the full pool reaches. The greedy path within the 21 peaks well before 21 and then falls; the sets chosen from the full pool reach further with fewer. Development folds, so the chosen sets are optimistic -- fig30 has the held-out view.

figures.title: Predictor value across the ANC ladder
figures.caption: Marginal value relative to the 21-predictor set (loss when dropped for members, marked [21]; gain when added for the rest), as a share of each rung's ceiling (full-pool AP minus prevalence). Sorted from most ANC1+-weighted to most ANC8+-weighted.

figures.title: The two prediction horizons on the same women
figures.caption: Held-out AUROC on the 984 ANC-entry women. Light = without early ANC, dark = with it, brown = the same sets fitted on the full cohort (before ANC). Paired intervals are in outputs/horizons/heldout_bootstrap.json.

figures.title: Value of early ANC initiation
figures.caption: Paired stratified-PSU bootstrap on the 984 held-out ANC-entry women.

figures.title: Every region, wartime vs post-war period
figures.caption: Pregnancies with at least 3 months inside the Tigray war window vs those conceived after the ceasefire, in every region. Sorted by the ANC4+ change.
